AUD crushed as Fed fails 'Warshach test'; $122m mysterious trade ahead of Fed decision signals FX volatility
WA exploration surge: Dalaroo copper-nickel-PGE targets, Critica 58% rare earths carbonate, Augustus 30g/t gold
IMF urges Australia to cut spending ahead of another RBA rate hike; states face soaring interest costs
Anthropic secures $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, boosting tech/infrastructure sentiment
Fuel/diesel cost crisis at east-coast ports; Middle East oil shock risk elevated
Qantas ground staff strike looms over 'Joyce-era' bargaining; consumer brands Cue and Veronika Maine face collapse
ACCC moves to break real estate monopoly; superannuation system under scrutiny

sectors.trend: Positive exploration momentum in WA: Dalaroo copper-nickel-PGE, Critica rare earths carbonate, Augustus gold targets. Oil price slide pressures energy but supports industrial metals demand.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX benefit from diversified commodity exposure. Junior explorers (Critica, Augustus) offer speculative upside. Iron ore stable; copper/rare earths narrative strengthens.

sectors.trend: Big four banks advancing on easing bond yields and supportive rate environment. IMF fiscal warning and state interest cost pressures create headwinds for sovereign credit.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX likely outperform. Net interest margin support from RBA hold. Monitor state debt servicing costs.

sectors.trend: Oil prices sliding, but Middle East shock risk (Trump 'little war') and diesel supply crunch at east-coast ports create volatility. Coal policy debate ongoing.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WDS.AX face margin pressure from diesel costs. LNG names (WDS, BHP) insulated. Coal policy uncertainty weighs on energy transition names.

sectors.trend: Weak: Cue and Veronika Maine face collapse; Coles keeps milk prices elevated; real wages growth crushed by exploited workers; Qantas strike risk.
sectors.implications: WOW.AX, WES.AX, COL.AX face margin and demand pressure. Qantas (QAN.AX) strike risk is a near-term catalyst. Consumer staples defensive positioning warranted.

sectors.trend: Anthropic $31bn QLD datacentre deal signals major AI infrastructure buildout. AI slowdown debate (Zuckerberg, Huang) keeps sentiment elevated. REAX weakness reflects AI-driven market shifts.
sectors.implications: ASX-listed datacentre/infrastructure plays and CSL.AX (healthcare tech) benefit. Global AI capex cycle supports sentiment but valuations stretched.

sectors.trend: ACCC targeting real estate monopoly; Trump policy mulls crashing Aussie house prices; tenants catching a break. Mixed signals.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face regulatory and policy risk. Housing affordability pressure may support rental demand but cap rate uncertainty persists.

key_themes: AUD weakness from Fed uncertainty and Trump trade policy
IMF fiscal tightening warning vs RBA rate path
WA mining exploration renaissance (copper, rare earths, gold)
Fuel/diesel cost crisis as structural issue, not supply
Consumer sector fragility: brand collapses, wage stagnation, Qantas strike

risk_assessment.risk_factor: AUD/USD volatility from Fed policy and Trump trade actions
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge FX exposure; monitor AUD/USD 0.65 support; diversify into USD-denominated assets
Maintain energy hedges; monitor Brent crude $80 trigger; favour LNG over oil-exposed names

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike + IMF fiscal tightening
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce duration in fixed income; favour floating-rate and short-dated bonds; watch state debt

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Qantas strike and consumer sector fragility
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight QAN.AX pre-strike; rotate to defensive staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Diesel/fuel supply crunch at east-coast ports
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor logistics costs; favour companies with fuel hedging; watch WES.AX distribution margins
Screen counterparty exposure; avoid small-cap credit-linked positions

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight WA exploration juniors on copper/rare earths/gold discovery momentum
opportunities.rationale: Dalaroo, Critica, Augustus results signal a WA exploration upcycle; rare earths and copper align with global energy transition demand

opportunities.recommendation: Add to big four bank positions on easing yields and NIM support
opportunities.rationale: Banks advancing on bond yield easing; RBA hold provides margin stability; dividend yield attractive

opportunities.recommendation: Position in AI infrastructure and datacentre beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: Anthropic $31bn QLD deal signals multi-year capex cycle; ASX-listed infrastructure and power names benefit

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce Qantas and consumer discretionary exposure ahead of strike
defensive_moves.rationale: Qantas ground staff strike risk; consumer brands (Cue, Veronika Maine) collapsing; real wages under pressure

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD weakness and reduce long AUD duration
defensive_moves.rationale: AUD crushed on Fed failure; Trump policy risk; $122m speculative trade signals FX instability

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain energy hedges and favour LNG over oil-exposed names
defensive_moves.rationale: Middle East oil shock risk; diesel supply crunch; coal policy uncertainty

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 (^AXJO) likely to extend gains on easing oil and bond yields, with banks leading. Qantas strike and consumer weakness cap upside. AUD volatility from Fed/Trump adds noise. Net: modest upside 1-2% over 1-3 months.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook constructive but uneven. WA mining exploration cycle, AI infrastructure capex, and bank earnings support index. Risks: RBA hike, IMF fiscal tightening, Middle East escalation, consumer fragility. Index likely range-bound with sector rotation favouring materials and financials over consumer.
key_catalysts: RBA rate decision and IMF fiscal review
WA exploration drill results (Augustus, Critica, Dalaroo)
watch_list: RBA cash rate and CPI print
